Oil Prices Fall on Iran-U.S. Diplomatic Hopes
Published: Mon, Nov 2 2026, 12:04 AM EST | Updated (fetched ~17:58 GMT)

As of 12:11 p.m. ET:
- Brent crude: Down 7.7% to $104.66/barrel
- West Texas Intermediate: Down 7.3% to $96.50/barrel

Oil markets experienced a sharp selloff following signals from both the U.S. and Iran that diplomatic resolution may be possible after eight months of conflict-related disruption.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that President Trump "hasn't made a decision" on military action and expressed preference for peaceful resolution, saying "we would prefer to do it peacefully."

Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian indicated Tehran seeks dialogue to resolve issues, noting the Supreme Leader has authorized the government to pursue this path. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated an agreement is achievable if Washington "demonstrates goodwill" and "truly seeks a peaceful solution."

However, Ayatollah Khamenei called for Iran's armed forces to meet threats with "an immediate, impactful response."

Ryan McKay of TD Securities noted the recent price gains reflected anticipated escalation risk. While diplomatic discussions impact pricing, he cautioned that "so long as there is no concrete conclusion to the war...we do not anticipate a complete erosion of the risk premium."
